neighbours.label: The second piece of a few specific compounds: sock|eye (strongest), Song|bird, Opera| House; not ' eye', 'bird' or ' House' elsewhere
fire: Each July the lake turns red with spawning sockeye and the bears arrive.
The cannery packed mostly sockeye during the war years.
A lone songbird sang from the hedge all afternoon.
Our ferry passed the Sydney Opera House just before sunset.
Smoked sockeye was served on rye with dill.
The Royal Opera House reopened after a long restoration.
Fishermen say the sockeye run was late this season.
Her album Songbird sold a million copies.
quiet: Each July the lake turns red with spawning trout and the bears arrive.
The cannery packed mostly herring during the war years.
A lone mockingbird sang from the hedge all afternoon.
Our ferry passed the Sydney Harbour Bridge just before sunset.
Smoked mackerel was served on rye with dill.
The Royal Albert Hall reopened after a long restoration.
He lost a sock and got something in his eye this morning.
Her album Songwriter sold a million copies.

notes: Card: 'eye'/'e' after 'sock'/'Sockey', ' House' after 'Opera', 'bird' after 'Song', 'y' after 'Pose'. Probes: sockeye 1.15 / 0.92, Opera House 0.60, Songbird 0.46 / 0.31, Posey 0.24, lower-case opera house 0.16; halibut, blackbird, White House, a plain ' eye', bird's-eye, songwriter 0.00-0.01. A list: I found no shared pattern beyond 'second piece after a So-/O- first piece'.
